title: Challenges in probing turbulent and magnetic support in cores: The W43-MM1 protocluster case study
question: Quantify the kinetic and magnetic support operating within the cores of the high-mass protocluster W43-MM1 and test the simple assumptions behind the approximated virial theorem.

data.bands: 1.3 mm (continuum and lines) and ~3 mm (91.971 GHz line)
data.sensitivity: W43-Main mosaic (mJy/beam): sigma_I=3.86, sigma_Q=0.11, sigma_U=0.12, sigma_P=0.11; W43-SW mosaic (mJy/beam): sigma_I=0.53, sigma_Q=0.04, sigma_U=0.04, sigma_P=0.04

what.value: Core catalog (coordinates, sizes, 1.3 mm integrated fluxes) and bsens-denoised 1.3 mm continuum map

evidence.quote: We make use of the core catalog provided in (cite: Motte2018) and further extended in (cite: Nony2023) with a mass completness of 1.6 $M_\odot$.

we measured the integrated 1.3 mm flux within the previously defined area (i.e., the three-beam area with pixels from the central core and neighboring cores removed) using the bsens–denoised continuum map from (cite: Nony2023).

what.value: Classification of cores into prestellar and protostellar (using outflows and hot cores)

evidence.quote: The nature of cores was defined in (cite: Nony2020) leading to the detection of 27 protostellar cores using protostellar outflows by studying the CO (2–1) and SiO (5–4) lines and the hot cores identified by (cite: Brouillet2022) and (cite: Bonfand2024).
For this work, we consider core #14 as prestellar, following (cite: Valeille-Manet2025), due to its insufficient evidence of association with an outflow.

what.value: Core temperatures, masses, sizes, and protostellar luminosities; 2.5'' scale dust temperatures

evidence.quote: The core temperatures, masses and protostellar luminosities have been estimated by (cite: Motte2025) and span the 0.3-115 $M_\odot$ and 0.14-12.21$\times 10^3\,L_\odot$ ranges.
For this conversion, we adopt the dust temperature ($T_{\mathrm{dust}}$) derived by (cite: Dell’Ova2023) at a spatial scale of $2.5^{\prime\prime}$ and listed in (cite: Motte2025):

what.value: Magnetic field-density power-law scaling exponent beta = 0.53 (+0.09/-0.07) from Zeeman measurements

evidence.quote: For that, we compute each core density using their mass and size, and we apply the field–density relation, $B \, \propto\, n^{\beta}$ with $\beta = 0.53^{+0.09}_{-0.07}$ (cite: Whitworth2025).

recipe.goal: Create Stokes I, Q, U mosaics and debiased linear polarization and magnetic field angle maps
recipe.method: Combine three pointings for MM1-Main and two pointings for MM1-SW using CASA tclean in mosaic mode; compute linear polarization P, debias using Hull & Plambeck (2015) for <=5 sigma_P and sqrt(Q^2 + U^2 - sigma_P^2) for >5 sigma_P; compute polarization angle chi = 0.5 arctan(U/Q) and rotate by 90 deg to get B_POS orientation above 3 sigma_P.
key_parameters: 3 sigma_P threshold for plotting and selecting polarization vectors; 5 sigma_P transition between low-SNR and high-SNR debiasing
assumptions: Radiative alignment torque (RAT) mechanism aligns oblate dust grains with short axis along B field so thermal dust polarization is perpendicular to B_POS

recipe.goal: Measure core-scale velocity dispersions via On-Off spectral extraction and Gaussian fitting
recipe.method: Extract On spectrum (mean within core elliptical area) and Off spectrum (mean in annulus of 2.5 to 3.5 times getsf source size, masking overlapping neighboring cores); fit a single Gaussian following the hierarchy: DCN(3-2) On-Off -> 13CS(5-4) On-Off -> DCN(3-2) On -> 13CS(5-4) On, and use CH3CN(5_3-4_3) for hot cores #1 and #4; scale 13CS velocity dispersions by 0.98/1.28 to match DCN.
key_parameters: Off annulus inner/outer radii = 2.5 and 3.5 times getsf source size; 13CS to DCN scaling factor = 0.98/1.28
assumptions: Vicinity of each core in the annulus is representative of its local environment; gas temperature equals dust temperature (full thermalization); molecular weights mu = 28 (DCN), 45 (13CS), 41 (CH3CN)

recipe.goal: Measure three-beam scale polarization angle dispersion, surrounding gas density, and gradient-corrected velocity dispersion
recipe.method: In a circular three-beam area (diameter 3.6 x beam major axis, ~2.3'' / ~12,500 au) centered on each core with >=20 polarization semi-vectors (sampled at 4 semi-vectors per beam above 3 sigma_P), compute angle dispersion sigma_theta from Stokes Q and U (Eq. 3). Mask central and neighboring cores from the three-beam area; extract spectrum, fit single Gaussian, and subtract in quadrature both the standard deviation of the moment-1 velocity map within the mask and the thermal velocity dispersion. Measure integrated 1.3 mm flux in the same masked area from the Nony et al. (2023) bsens-denoised continuum map to compute mass M_3beam (Eq. 4) and volume density.
key_parameters: Three-beam diameter = 3.6 x beam major axis (~2.3'', ~12500 au); sampling = 4 semi-vectors per beam; minimum 20 semi-vectors above 3 sigma_P
assumptions: Distance d = 5.5 kpc; dust+gas mass opacity kappa_1.3mm = 0.01 cm^2 g^-1 (Ossenkopf & Henning 1994) assuming gas-to-dust ratio of 100; 2.5'' dust temperatures from Dell'Ova et al. (2023) / Motte et al. (2025); mean of spherical and oblate ellipsoidal geometries for density

recipe.goal: Estimate plane-of-sky magnetic field strength B_POS at three-beam scale and extrapolate to core scale
recipe.method: Apply the classical Davis-Chandrasekhar-Fermi (DCF) equation B_POS = Q * sqrt(4 pi rho) * sigma_v,NT / sigma_theta (Eq. 2) with Q = 0.5 at the three-beam scale, then extrapolate to core scales (~2500 au) using the core volume density and the empirical scaling B proportional to n^beta with beta = 0.53 (+0.09/-0.07).
key_parameters: DCF correction factor Q = 0.5; density scaling exponent beta = 0.53 (+0.09/-0.07) (mean uncertainty 0.08 used for error propagation)
assumptions: Isotropic turbulent motions; DCF reliability regime sigma_theta < 25 deg (cores #3, #4, #5, #9 with sigma_theta > 25 deg retained for statistics); spherical symmetry for core densities

recipe.goal: Compute virial parameters, mass-to-flux ratios, and contaminant infall velocities
recipe.method: Calculate kinetic virial parameter alpha_kin (Eq. 5), mass-to-magnetic-flux ratio lambda_B (Eq. 6), magnetic virial mass M_phi (Eq. 7), and total virial parameter alpha_vir,B (Eq. 8). For the 11 protostellar cores with both estimates and alpha_vir,B > 1, compute the contaminant velocity that must be subtracted to bring them to alpha_vir,B = 1, and test reducing non-thermal support by a factor of two.
key_parameters: Density profile power-law index p = 0 for prestellar cores and p = 2 for protostellar cores; core radius R = FWHM^dec
assumptions: Simplified virial theorem limited to volume terms (neglecting surface terms); central protostellar mass neglected (Class 0-like envelopes dominate); cylindrical geometry for mean column density <N_H2>
